evals.prompt: 커밋해줘. 인증 미들웨어 버그 수정하고 새 rate-limit 설정도 같이 넣었어.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the tree, splits the bug fix and the new setting into separate Conventional Commits, shows the plan, and creates them one at a time with explicit paths.
assertions: A fix and a feature are not combined into one commit.
The commit plan is shown before the first commit is created.
Only explicit paths are staged; `git add .` and `git add -A` are not used.
Each commit subject follows the Conventional Commits format with a truthful type.

evals.prompt: Commit everything in the tree. It includes a new `.env` with our staging database password and an `.env.example` template.
evals.expected_output: Excludes the `.env` file, warns that it looks like a secret, and commits the `.env.example` template because that exact basename is a public template.
assertions: The `.env` file is excluded by default and reported as a suspected secret.
The exact basename `.env.example` is not excluded solely for matching `.env*`.
The user is asked to confirm before any suspected secret is committed.

evals.prompt: My last four commit subjects are a mess — `wip`, `fix stuff`, `更新`, `asdf`. Turn them into Conventional Commits.
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as a history rewrite rather than new commits and hands off to git-commit-rewrite instead of creating commits.
assertions: Existing commit messages are not rewritten by this workflow.
The request is routed to `git-commit-rewrite` by name.
No destructive history command is run from this skill.

evals.prompt: The pre-commit hook keeps failing on formatting. Just commit with --no-verify so we can move on.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to bypass the hook, fixes the formatting failure it reports, and re-runs the hook before committing.
assertions: The underlying hook failure is fixed rather than skipped.
The commit is created only after the hook passes.
